events.summary: The Census Bureau published a notice requesting 60 days of public comment on the proposed reinstatement, with modifications, of the Local Update of Census Addresses (LUCA) operation prior to submitting the information collection request to OMB for approval. LUCA enables tribal, state, and local governments to review and comment on the Census Address List for their jurisdictions before the 2030 decennial census. events.title: Border Patrol dropped blind refugee miles from home without notification
events.summary: On February 19, Border Patrol agents dropped Nurul Amin Shah Alam, a nearly blind legal refugee from genocide in Myanmar who spoke no English and could not read, write, or use electronic devices, miles from his home in Buffalo, New York. Agents did not notify his lawyer or family of the drop-off. When his family filed a missing persons report, police believed Shah Alam was still with Border Patrol and closed the file. He was found dead on the street on February 24. A Customs and Border Protection spokesperson claimed agents had offered Shah Alam a "courtesy ride" to a coffee shop near his last known address and that he "showed no signs of distress, mobility issues or disabilities requiring special assistance."
events.why_relevant: The death of a vulnerable legal refugee in government custody, combined with lack of notification to family or counsel and apparent misrepresentation of his condition, raises serious questions about duty of care and accountability in immigration enforcement.

events.title: Supreme Court ruled tariffs exceeded presidential authority under IEEPA
events.summary: The Supreme Court issued a 6-3 decision invalidating many of Trump's tariffs, holding that he exceeded his authority under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA), a 1977 law reserved for national emergencies. Chief Justice John Roberts authored the majority opinion, joined by three liberal justices and two conservative justices (Neil Gorsuch and Amy Coney Barrett). The ruling invalidated reciprocal tariffs (ranging from 34% on China to 10% baseline) and a 25% tariff on goods from Canada, China, and Mexico imposed on fentanyl grounds. Trump could seek to reimpose tariffs using other laws. The decision does not affect all tariffs.
events.why_relevant: The ruling reasserts congressional authority over taxation and tariffs, reaffirming separation of powers and limiting unilateral executive economic power.
events.basis: The Supreme Court delivered a major blow to Trump, ruling that he exceeded his authority when imposing sweeping tariffs using a law reserved for a national emergency.

events.title: Supreme Court rules Trump's unilateral tariffs unconstitutional
events.summary: The Supreme Court struck down Trump's use of the International Emergency Economic Powers Act to impose sweeping tariffs on countries worldwide. Chief Justice John Roberts, writing for the majority, held that the Constitution vests taxation authority exclusively in Congress, not the presidency. The decision may require the administration to return $175–200 billion in tariffs collected from U.S. businesses and consumers without congressional approval.

events.basis: The Supreme Court struck down Trump's attempt to impose sweeping tariffs on countries around the world by unilaterally declaring 'emergencies' to justify them. events.title: Trump issues executive order continuing suspension of duty-free de minimis treatment for all imports
events.summary: President Trump issued an executive order on February 20, 2026, continuing the suspension of duty-free de minimis treatment under 19 U.S.C. 1321(a)(2)(C) for all countries. The order modifies prior tariff directives and establishes that U.S. Customs and Border Protection shall collect duties on all shipments, including those sent through the international postal network, effective February 24, 2026. The duty rate applied equals the temporary import surcharge established by a concurrent proclamation issued the same day.

events.title: Trump revokes tariff duties imposed under emergency powers
events.summary: President Trump issued an executive order on February 20, 2026, terminating additional ad valorem duties (tariffs) that had been imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) in nine prior executive orders addressing alleged threats from China, Brazil, Russia, Iran, Cuba, and illicit drug flows. The order directs executive agencies to immediately cease collection of these tariffs while preserving the underlying national emergency declarations and all other tariff actions under different statutory authorities (Section 232 and Section 301).
events.why_relevant: The order reverses a core Trump trade policy tool—emergency tariffs—signaling a shift in trade strategy and demonstrating executive authority to unilaterally modify economic coercion mechanisms without legislative input.
